LINEAR CORE (17 direct input->output edges on z-scored inputs): ca +2.16, slope:2 +1.08, sex:1 +0.85, sex:0 -0.48, cp:3 -0.76, chol +0.68, cp:1 -0.66, trestbps +0.57, thal:3 -0.54, oldpeak +0.53, fbs:1 -0.53, exang:1 +0.34, cp:4 +0.30, slope:1 -0.20, thalach -0.20, age +0.10, fbs:0 +0.01; inputs restecg:0, restecg:2, exang:0, slope:3, thal:4, thal:7 are unused (listed as entries only for coverage). For a typical patient it acts on, it lowers the predicted risk of heart disease from about 99% without this part to about 81% with it (on the training data only). The model has little data on this: only 15 training patients (patients the part acts on).
In the training data, 9 of these 15 patients had heart disease.
